reasoning: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is a well-documented scientific myth. Modern neuroimaging technologies, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) scans, show that virtually all parts of the brain are active throughout the day, even during sleep or simple tasks. There is no large "dormant" or "untapped" area of the brain. Furthermore, from an evolutionary perspective, the brain is an energy-intensive organ (consuming about 20% of the body's energy); keeping 90% of it unused would be highly inefficient, and unused brain tissue typically degenerates or atrophies over time.
title: Humans only use 10% of their brains
